title: Interactive Surface Lab: Figma SpriteLayer + Rollover Affordances for Compact Dashboards
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Compact dashboard cards in the Console currently lack a consistent hover/rollover language and layered surface treatment for dense cost views and rollout controls. Goal: Define a lightweight, accessible SpriteLayer pattern in Figma that supports compact metrics cards, inline rollout toggles, and low-latency affordances without increasing perceived visual noise. Scope: token mappings, surface elevation rules, hover states, transform/translate micro-animations, and a mini-pattern library (SpriteLayer variants) for handoff to frontend and motion engineering.
decisions: Use a three-layer SpriteLayer model: base (content), overlay (affordance icons + micro-controls), and transient (hover highlights).
Prefer opacity + translateY for hover transitions to avoid layout shift and preserve KV cache rendering assumptions in the Console runtime.
Limit elevation steps to two for compact cards to keep contrast predictable across themes and avoid shadow overlap with tooltips.
tradeoffs: Keeping elevation limited reduces visual depth but simplifies implementation across browsers and reduces CSS paint cost.
Using opacity/translate instead of scaling preserves text readability but is slightly less 'playful' visually; chosen for professional dashboards and accessibility.
Embedding affordances (e.g., rollout toggles) in overlay reduces click area for the main card; mitigated via explicit hit-target padding in the overlay spec.

acceptance_criteria: SpriteLayer Figma components (base/overlay/transient) are published in the DS Figma library with clear variant names and token references.
Prototype demonstrates hover and keyboard-focus states for compact metrics card and rollout toggle; interaction recorded in the Figma prototype.
Accessibility checklist completed: focus management, ARIA labels, contrast checks, and 44x44 touch target guidance applied.
Frontend PR creates CSS variables and a feature flag (spritelayer-experiment) and implements one example card in the cost-insights route for validation.
Performance notes: animations use will-change: transform, opacity, and fallback to instant state for flagged low-GPU environments.
